# Incident Report — MTA 2024-11-26 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host

| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.11.26.183 | Consistent source of all malicious traffic |
| MAC | d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b | `eth.src` on frames with `ip.src==10.11.26.183` (ARP-confirmed: `arp.src.proto_ipv4==10.11.26.183` → same MAC) |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-B8TQK49 (NetBIOS alias NEMOTODES) | NBNS name registrations `DESKTOP-B8TQK49<00>/<20>`, `NEMOTODES<00>/<1e>`, from 10.11.26.183; also self-issued DNS queries for `DESKTOP-B8TQK49` / `DESKTOP-B8TQK49.local` |
| Logged-in user | oboomwald | Kerberos `CNameString` field, TGS/AS exchanges between 10.11.26.183 and the domain controller 10.11.26.3 (NEMOTODES-DC.nemotoads.health) |

Domain: `nemotoads.health`, DC = 10.11.26.3 (NEMOTODE-DC / NEMOTODES-DC).

## Malware Family

**NetSupport RAT** — a commercial remote-access tool (legitimate NetSupport Manager) trojanized and repurposed as commodity malware.

**Attribution: signature-confirmed.** Suricata/ET fired multiple exact-match signatures on the C2 traffic:
- `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity`
- `ETPRO TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin`
- `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin` / `Response`

This is independently confirmed at the protocol level: the client-to-C2 POST requests carry `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3` and a body that decodes from hex to the literal NetSupport client protocol:
```
CMD=POLL
INFO=1
ACK=1
```
and encrypted variants beginning `CMD=ENCD`, matching NetSupport's known polling/beacon format.

## Infection Chain (as observed)

1. **04:50:11 UTC** — 10.11.26.183 connects to `classicgrand.com` (213.246.109.5:443), the initial redirector/lure landing page.
2. **04:50:14 UTC** — DNS lookup and connection to `modandcrackedapk.com` (193.42.38.139:443) — a fake cracked-software/mod-APK download site (flagged `ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain`). This is the largest single conversation in the capture (≈11 MB over TLS), consistent with delivery of the RAT payload over an encrypted channel that cannot be decoded from this capture without TLS keys.
3. **04:50:45 UTC** — the infected host begins beaconing to the NetSupport RAT C2 at **194.180.191.64:443** with repeated `POST /fakeurl.htm` requests (plaintext HTTP carried on port 443, not actual TLS — flagged `ET POLICY HTTP traffic on port 443 (POST)` / `HTTP POST on unusual Port Possibly Hostile`).
4. The malware also performs a geolocation lookup against the legitimate NetSupport infrastructure (`geo.netsupportsoftware.com`, GET `/location/loca.asp`), a known NetSupport client self-check behavior and further corroboration of the family.

Note: SMB/EFSRPC/NetBIOS activity from 10.11.26.183 to the domain controller (10.11.26.3) at 04:49:55–04:50:10 UTC (`MS-EFSR EfsRpcOpenFileRaw`, SMBv1, IPC$ access) occurs *before* the malicious DNS/TLS chain begins and is grouped with routine AD/Group Policy client traffic to the DC — treated as benign context, not an IOC, absent further evidence of exploitation.

## Indicators of Compromise

### C2 endpoints
| Type | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| C2 endpoint | **194.180.191.64:443** | Repeated `POST /fakeurl.htm` with `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3`, decoded `CMD=POLL/ENCD` protocol bodies; Suricata `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity` / `Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin` |

### Malicious domains
| Type | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Domain | **modandcrackedapk.com** (resolves to 193.42.38.139) | DNS query from victim + TLS SNI `modandcrackedapk.com`; Suricata `ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain in DNS Lookup` and `... in TLS SNI` |
| Domain | **classicgrand.com** (resolves to 213.246.109.5) | TLS SNI `classicgrand.com`, first-stage redirector contacted immediately before the modandcrackedapk.com lookup; 3.5 MB conversation |

### Malicious URLs
| Type | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| URL | **http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm** | Direct HTTP request/response capture, NetSupport RAT beacon endpoint |

### Files
No malware executable/dropper could be extracted from this capture — the payload delivery from `modandcrackedapk.com` (193.42.38.139) occurred entirely inside a TLS session, which cannot be decoded without session keys, so no file name or hash can be grounded for the initial dropper. `--export-objects http` over the full capture yielded only benign/protocol artifacts (Windows connectivity check, Adobe update-checker text file, NetSupport geolocation response, and the RAT's own poll/ack bodies) — none of these represent a malicious payload.

## Benign Context (not IOCs)
- `www.msftconnecttest.com`, `ctldl.windowsupdate.com`, Adobe (`acroipm2.adobe.com`), Microsoft/Office/MSN/Bing/OneDrive telemetry domains, Google Maps/Fonts, `code.jquery.com`, `login.live.com`, `r10.o.lencr.org` (OCSP) — standard OS/browser/software background traffic.
- `confirmsubscription.com`, `default.exp-tas.com` — ad-tech/tracking domains seen in the same browsing session as the malicious redirect chain; not confirmed as part of the infection path in this capture, listed here only for completeness rather than as IOCs.
- Domain-controller SMB/EFSRPC/Kerberos/LDAP traffic to 10.11.26.3 — routine AD client activity.

## Summary

The Windows workstation **DESKTOP-B8TQK49 (10.11.26.183, MAC d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b)**, logged in as domain user **oboomwald** on the `nemotoads.health` domain, was infected with **NetSupport RAT** (signature-confirmed) after browsing through a redirect chain (`classicgrand.com` → the fake cracked-software site `modandcrackedapk.com`) around 04:50 UTC on 2024-11-26. The malware immediately began beaconing to its C2 at **194.180.191.64:443** via HTTP POST to `/fakeurl.htm` using the NetSupport client protocol, confirmed by both the User-Agent string, the decoded protocol body, and matching ET/ETPRO Suricata signatures. The initial payload could not be recovered from the capture because delivery occurred over TLS.
